nodes.name: Advertising-data (soso.com) experiment
nodes.statement: Predicting whether a user of a search engine will click on an advertisement presented to him or her is of central importance to the business of several internet companies, and in this section, we present experiments studying the performance of the \avgm\ and \savgm\ methods for this task. umobs - \optvar^*]}^2 &\leq  rac{ eta^2}{
umobs^{3/2}}. \end{align} \end{subequations} Before proving the theorem, we introduce some notation and a few preliminary results. Let $\gradient_t = 
abla f(\optvar^t; \statrv_t)$ be the gradient of the $t^{th}$ sample in stochastic gradient descent, where we consider running SGD on a single machine. We also let  egin{equation*} \project(v) \defeq \argmin_{\optvar \in \optvarspace} \left\{ \ltwo{\optvar - v}^2 ight\} \end{equation*} denote the projection of the point $v$ onto the domain $\optvarspace$. We now state a known result, which gives sharp rates on the convergence of the iterates $\{\optvar^t\}$ in stochastic gradient descent.  egin{lemma}[\citeauthor{RakhlinShSr12}, \citeyear{RakhlinShSr12}] Assume that $\E[\ltwo{\gradient_t}^2] \leq \lipobj^2$ for all $t$. Choosing $\eta_t= rac{c}{\lambda t}$ for some $c\geq 1$, for any $t \in \N$ we have  egin{equation*} \E\left[\ltwo{\optvar^t-\optvar^*}^2ight] \leq  rac{\alpha \lipobj^2}{\lambda^2t} ~~~ \mbox{where} ~~~ \alpha = 4c^2. \end{equation*} \end{lemma} \vspace*{.1in} With these ingredients, we can now turn to the proof of Theorem~ef{theorem:sgd}. Lemma~ef{lemma:sgd-distance-bound} gives the inequality~\eqref{eqn:sgd-bound-part1}, so it remains to prove that $\optavg^
umobs$ has the smaller bound~\eqref{eqn:sgd-bound-part2} on its bias. To that end, recall the neighborhood $U_ho \subset \optvarspace$ in Assumption~ef{assumption:smoothness-sgd}, and note that  egin{align*} \optvar^{t + 1} - \optvar^* & = \project(\optvar^t - \eta_t \gradient_t - \optvar^*) \ & = \optvar^t - \eta_t \gradient_t - \optvar^* + \indic{\optvar^{t+1} 
ot\in U_ho} \left(\project(\optvar^t - \eta_t \gradient_t) - (\optvar^t - \eta_t \gradient_t)ight) \end{align*} since when $\optvar \in U_ho$, we have $\project(\optvar) = \optvar$. Consequently, an application of the triangle inequality gives  egin{equation*} \ltwo{\E[\optvar^{t+1}-\optvar^*]} \leq \ltwo{\E[\optvar^{t}-\eta_t\gradient_t-\optvar^*]} + \E[\ltwo{(\Pi(\optvar^{t}-\eta_t\gradient_t) -(\optvar^{t}-\eta_t\gradient_t))1(\optvar^{t+1}
otin U_ho)}]. \end{equation*} By the definition of the projection and the fact that $\optvar^t \in \optvarspace$, we additionally have  egin{equation*} \ltwo{\project(\optvar^{t}-\eta_t\gradient_t) -(\optvar^{t}-\eta_t\gradient_t)} \le \ltwo{\optvar^{t}-(\optvar^{t}-\eta_t\gradient_t))} \le \eta_t \ltwo{g_t}. \end{equation*} Thus, by applying H"older's inequality (with the conjugate choices $(p, q) = (4,  rac{4}{3})$) and Assumption~ef{assumption:smoothness-sgd}, we have  egin{align} \ltwo{\E[\optvar^{t+1}-\optvar^*]} & \le \ltwo{\E[\optvar^{t}-\eta_t\gradient_t-\optvar^*]} + \eta_t \E[\ltwo{\gradient_t} \indic{\optvar^{t + 1} 
ot\in U_ho}] 
onumber \ & \le \ltwo{\E[\optvar^{t}-\eta_t\gradient_t-\optvar^*]} + \eta_t \sqrt[4]{\E[\ltwo{\gradient_t}^4]} \left(\E[\indic{\optvar^t 
ot\in U_ho}^{4/3}]ight)^{3/4} 
onumber \ & \le \ltwo{\E[\optvar^{t}-\eta_t\gradient_t-\optvar^*]} + \eta_t \lipobj \left(\P(\optvar^t 
ot\in U_ho)ight)^{3/4} 
onumber \ & \le \ltwo{\E[\optvar^{t}-\eta_t\gradient_t-\optvar^*]} + \eta_t \lipobj \left( rac{\E\ltwo{\optvar^{t+1}-\optvar^*}^2}{ho^2}ight)^{3/4}, \end{align} the inequality~\eqref{eqn:sgd-tplusone-truncation} following from an application of Markov's inequality. By applying Lemma~ef{lemma:sgd-distance-bound}, we finally obtain  egin{align} \ltwo{\E[\optvar^{t + 1} - \optvar^*]} & \le \ltwo{\E[\optvar^t - \eta_t \gradient_t - \optvar^*]} + \eta_t \lipobj \left( rac{\alpha \lipobj^2}{\strongparam^2 ho^2 t}ight)^{3/4} 
onumber \ & = \ltwo{\E[\optvar^t - \eta_t \gradient_t - \optvar^*]} +  rac{c \alpha^{3/4} \lipobj^{5/2}}{ \strongparam^{5/2} ho^{3/2}} \cdot  rac{1}{t^{7/4}}. \end{align} Now we turn to controlling the rate at which $\optvar^t - \eta_t \gradient_t$ goes to zero. Let $f_t(\cdot) = f(\cdot; \statrv_t)$ be shorthand for the loss evaluated on the $t^{th}$ data point. By defining  egin{align*} r_t = g_t - 
abla f_t(\optvar^*) - 
abla^2 f_t(\optvar^*)(\optvar^t - \optvar^*), \end{align*} a bit of algebra yields  egin{equation*} \gradient_t = 
abla f_t(\optvar^*) + 
abla^2 f_t(\optvar^*)(\optvar^t-\optvar^*) + r_t. \end{equation*} Since $\optvar^t$ belongs to the $\sigma$-field of $\statrv_1, \ldots, \statrv_{t-1}$, the Hessian $
abla^2 f_t(\optvar^*)$ is (conditionally) independent of $\optvar^t$ and  egin{equation} \E[\gradient_t] = 
abla^2 F_0(\optvar^*)\E[\optvar^t-\optvar^*] + \E[r_t \indic{\optvar^t\in U_ho}] + \E[r_t\indic{\optvar^t
otin U_ho}]. \end{equation} If $\optvar^t\in U_ho$, then Taylor's theorem implies that $r_t$ is the Lagrange remainder  egin{align*} r_t = (

abla^2 f_t(\optvar^*))(\optvar'-\optvar^*), \end{align*} where $\optvar'= \interp\optvar^t +(1-\interp)\optvar^*$ for some $\interp \in [0, 1]$. Applying Assumption~ef{assumption:smoothness-sgd} and H"older's inequality, we find that since $\optvar^t$ is conditionally independent of $\statrv_t$,  egin{align*} \E\left[\ltwo{r_t \indic{\optvar^t \in U_ho}}ight] & \le \E\left[ \matrixnorm{
abla^2 f(\optvar'; \statrv_t) -

ot \in U_ho$, we have the following sequence of inequalities:  egin{align*} \lefteqn{\E\left[\ltwo{r_t \indic{\optvar^t 
ot\in U_ho}}ight] \stackrel{(i)}{\le} \sqrt[4]{\E[\ltwo{r_t}^4]} \left(\P(\optvar^t 
ot \in U_ho)ight)^{3/4}} \ & \qquad\qquad\quad ~ \stackrel{(ii)}{\le} \sqrt[4]{ 3^3\left(\E[\ltwo{\gradient_t}^4] + \E[\ltwo{
abla f_t(\optvar^*)}^4] + \E[\ltwo{
abla^2 f_t(\optvar^*)(\optvar^t - \optvar^*)}^4]ight)} \left(\P(\optvar^t 
ot \in U_ho)ight)^{3/4} \ & \qquad\qquad\quad ~\le 3^{3/4} \sqrt[4]{\lipobj^4 + \lipobj^4 + \lipgrad^4 adius^4} \left(\P(\optvar^t 
ot \in U_ho)ight)^{3/4} \ & \qquad\qquad\quad \stackrel{(iii)}{\le} 3(\lipobj + \lipgrad adius) \left( rac{\alpha \lipobj^2}{\strongparam^2 ho^2 t}ight)^{3/4}. \end{align*} Here step~(i) follows from H"older's inequality (again applied with the conjugates $(p, q) = (4,  rac{4}{3})$); step~(ii) follows from Jensen's inequality, since $(a + b + c)^4 \le 3^3(a^4 + b^4 + c^4)$; and step~(iii) follows from Markov's inequality, as in the bounds~\eqref{eqn:sgd-tplusone-truncation} and~\eqref{eqn:sgd-t-plus-one-mean-square}. Combining our two bounds on $r_t$, we find that  egin{equation} \E[\ltwo{r_t}] \le  rac{\alpha \liphessian \lipobj^2}{\strongparam^2 t} +  rac{3 \alpha^{3/4} \lipobj^{3/2} (\lipobj + \lipgrad adius)}{ \strongparam^{3/2} ho^{3/2}} \cdot  rac{1}{t^{3/4}}. \end{equation} By combining the expansion~\eqref{eqn:sgd-truncate-grad} with the bound~\eqref{eqn:sgd-rt-bound}, we find that  egin{align*} \lefteqn{\ltwo{\E[\optvar^t - \eta_t \gradient_t - \optvar^*]} = \ltwo{\E[(I - \eta_t 
abla^2 F_0(\optvar^*))(\optvar^t - \optvar^*) + \eta_t r_t]}} \ & \qquad \qquad \le \ltwo{\E[(I - \eta_t 
abla^2 F_0(\optvar^*))(\optvar^t - \optvar^*)]} +  rac{c \alpha \liphessian \lipobj^2}{\strongparam^3 t^2} +  rac{3 c \alpha^{3/4} \lipobj^{3/2} (\lipobj + \lipgrad adius)}{ \strongparam^{5/2} ho^{3/2}} \cdot  rac{1}{t^{7/4}}. \end{align*} Using the earlier bound~\eqref{eqn:sgd-t-plus-one-mean-square}, this inequality then yields  egin{equation*} \ltwo{\E[\optvar^{t + 1} - \optvar^*]} \le \matrixnorm{I - \eta_t 
abla^t F_0(\optvar^*)}_2 \ltwo{\E[\optvar^t - \optvar^*]} +  rac{c \alpha^{3/4} \lipobj^{3/2}}{\strongparam^{5/2} t^{7/4}} \!\left( rac{\alpha^{1/4}\liphessian \lipobj^{1/2}}{\strongparam^{1/2} t^{1/4}} +  rac{4 \lipobj + \lipgrad adius}{ho^{3/2}}ight)\!. \end{equation*} We now complete the proof via an inductive argument using our immediately preceding bounds. Our reasoning follows a similar induction given by~\citet{RakhlinShSr12}. First, note that by strong convexity and our condition that $\matrixnorm{
abla^2 F_0(\optvar^*)} \le \lipgrad$, we have  egin{equation*} \matrixnorm{I - \eta_t 
abla^2 F_0(\optvar^*)} = 1 - \eta_t \lambda_{\min}(
abla^2 F_0(\optvar^*) \le 1 - \eta_t \strongparam \end{equation*} whenever $1 - \eta_t \lipgrad \ge 0$. nodes.name: Remark: bias-correction intuition for SAVGM
nodes.statement: The intuition for the weighted estimator~\eqref{eqn:bootstrap-avg-def} is similar to that for standard bias correction procedures using the bootstrap or subsampling~\citep{EfronTi93,Hall92, PolitisRoWo99}. Roughly speaking, if $b_0 = \optvar^* - \optvar_1$ is the bias of the first estimator, then we may approximate $b_0$ by the subsampled estimate of bias $b_1 = \optvar^* - \optvar_2$. Then, we use the fact that $b_1 \approx b_0 / \ratio$ to argue that $\optvar^* \approx (\optvar_1 - \ratio \optvar_2) / (1-\ratio)$. The re-normalization enforces that the relative ``weights'' of $\optavg_1$ and $\optavg_2$ sum to 1. \\

nodes.name: Multiple subsamples / resampling with replacement
nodes.statement: In practice, an optimal choice of $\ratio$ may not be apparent, which may necessitate cross validation or another type of model evaluation. We leave as intriguing open questions whether computing multiple subsamples at each machine can yield improved performance or reduce the variance of the \savgm\ procedure, and whether using estimates based on resampling the data with replacement, as opposed to without replacement as considered here, can yield improved performance.

nodes.statement: a bootstrap correction is possible for the stochastic-gradient based estimator; such a correction could be significant, because the term $\beta^2 / \numobs^{3/2}$ arising from the bias in the stochastic gradient estimator may be non-trivial. We leave this question to future work.

nodes.name: Nonparametric / efficiency-communication interplay
nodes.statement: remain open after this work. First, nonparametric estimation problems, which often suffer superlinear scaling in the size of the data, may provide an interesting avenue for further study of decomposition-based methods. Our own recent work has addressed aspects of this challenge in the context of kernel methods for non-parametric regression~\citep{ZhaDucWai_COLT13}. More generally, an understanding of the interplay between statistical efficiency and communication could provide an avenue for further research, and it may also be interesting to study the effects of subsampled or bootstrap-based estimators in other distributed environments.

nodes.statement: \item[(1)] As shown in the proof of Theorem~\ref{theorem:no-bootstrap}, with high probability, the empirical risk $F_1$ is strongly convex in a ball $B_\rho(\optvar_1)$ of constant radius $\rho > 0$ around $\optvar_1$. onumber \ & \le  rac{1}{m} \E[\ltwo{\optvar_1 - \optvar^*}^2] + \ltwo{\E[\optvar_1 - \optvar^*]}^2. \end{align} Here we used the definition of the averaged vector $\optavg$ and the fact that for $i 
eq j$, the vectors $\optvar_i$ and $\optvar_j$ are statistically independent, they are functions of independent samples. The upper bound~\eqref{eqn:error-inequality} illuminates the path for the remainder of our proof: we bound each of $\E[\ltwo{\optvar_i - \optvar^*}^2]$ and $\ltwo{\E[\optvar_i - \optvar^*]}^2$. Intuitively, since our objective is locally strongly convex by Assumption~ef{assumption:strong-convexity}, the empirical minimizing vector $\optvar_1$ is a nearly unbiased estimator for $\optvar^*$, which allows us to prove the convergence rates in the theorem.

nodes.name: Define good events and apply Lemma 1
Taylor expansion of the optimization error
nodes.statement:
Our approach from here is to give bounds on $\E[\ltwo{\optvar_1 - \optvar^*}^2]$ and $\ltwo{\E[\optvar_1 - \optvar^*]}^2$ by careful Taylor expansions, which allows us to bound $\E[\ltwo{\optavg_1 - \optvar^*}^2]$ via our initial expansion~\eqref{eqn:error-inequality}. We begin by noting that whenever the events $\event_0$, $\event_1$, and $\event_2$ hold, then $
abla F_1(\optvar_1) = 0$, and moreover, by a Taylor series expansion of $
abla F_1$ between $\optvar^*$ and $\optvar_1$, we have  egin{align*} 0 = 
abla F_1(\optvar_1) & = 
abla F_1(\optvar^*) + 
abla^2 F_1(\optvar')(\optvar_1 - \optvar^*) \end{align*} where $\optvar' = \interp \optvar^* + (1 - \interp) \optvar_1$ for some $\interp \in [0, 1]$. By adding and subtracting terms, we have  egin{multline} 0 = 
abla F_1(\optvar^*) + (
abla^2 F_1(\optvar') - 
abla^2 F_1(\optvar^*)) (\optvar_1 - \optvar^*) \ + (
abla^2 F_1(\optvar^*) - 
abla^2 F_0(\optvar^*))(\optvar_1 - \optvar^*) + 
abla^2 F_0(\optvar^*)(\optvar_1 - \optvar^*). \end{multline} Since $
abla^2 F_0(\optvar^*) \succeq \strongparam I$, we can define the inverse Hessian matrix $\invhessian \defeq [
abla^2 F_0(\optvar^*)]^{-1}$, and setting $\optvarerr \defeq \optvar_1 - \optvar^*$, we multiply both sides of the Taylor expansion~\eqref{eqn:taylor-error-expansion} by $\invhessian$ to obtain the relation  egin{equation} \optvarerr = -\invhessian 
abla F_1(\optvar^*) + \invhessian(
abla^2 F_1(\optvar^*) - 
abla^2 F_1(\optvar')) \optvarerr + \invhessian(
abla^2 F_0(\optvar^*) - 
abla^2 F_1(\optvar^*)) \optvarerr. \end{equation} Thus, if we define the matrices $P = 
abla^2 F_0(\optvar^*) - 
abla^2 F_1(\optvar^*)$ and $Q = 
abla^2 F_1(\optvar^*) - 
abla^2 F_1(\optvar')$, equality~\eqref{eqn:error-expansion} can be re-written as  egin{equation} \optvar_1 - \optvar^* = -\invhessian 
abla F_1(\optvar^*) + \invhessian(P + Q)(\optvar_1 - \optvar^*). \end{equation} Note that equation~\eqref{eqn:simple-error-expansion} holds when the conditions of Lemma~ef{lemma:good-events} hold, and otherwise we may simply assert only that $\ltwo{\optvar_1 - \optvar^*} \le adius$. Roughly, we expect the final two terms in the error expansion~\eqref{eqn:simple-error-expansion} to be of smaller order than the first term, since we hope that $\optvar_1 - \optvar^* ightarrow 0$ and additionally that the Hessian differences decrease to zero at a sufficiently fast rate. We now formalize this intuition.

nodes.statement:
\paragraph{Control of $\ltwo{\E[\optvar_1 - \optvar^*]}^2$:} It remains to consider the $\ltwo{\E[\optvar_1 - \optvar^*]}^2$ term from our initial error inequality~\eqref{eqn:error-inequality}. When the events~\eqref{eqn:good-events} occur, we know that all derivatives exist, so we may recursively apply our expansion~\eqref{eqn:simple-error-expansion} of $\optvar_1 - \optvar^*$ to find that  egin{align} \optvar_1 - \optvar^* & = -\invhessian
abla F_1(\optvar^*) + \invhessian(P + Q)(\optvar_1 - \optvar^*) 
onumber \ & = \underbrace{-\invhessian
abla F_1(\optvar^*) + \invhessian(P + Q)\left[-\invhessian 
abla F_1(\optvar^*) + \invhessian(P + Q)(\optvar_1 - \optvar^*)ight]}_{\eqdef v} \end{align} where we have introduced $v$ as shorthand for the vector on the right hand side. Thus, with a bit of algebraic manipulation we obtain the relation  egin{equation} \optvar_1 - \optvar^* = \indic{\event} v + \indic{\event^c} (\optvar_1 - \optvar^*) = v + \indic{\event^c}(\optvar_1 - \optvar^*) - \indic{\event^c}v = v + \indic{\event^c}(\optvar_1 - \optvar^* - v). \end{equation} Now note that $\E[
abla F_1(\optvar^*)]=0$ thus  egin{align*} \E[v] & = \E\left[-\invhessian 
abla F_1(\optvar^*) + \invhessian(P + Q)[-\invhessian 
abla F_1(\optvar^*) + \invhessian(P + Q)(\optvar_1 - \optvar^*)]ight] \ & = \E\left[\invhessian(P + Q)\invhessian\left[(P + Q)(\optvar_1 - \optvar^*) - 
abla F_1(\optvar^*)ight]ight]. \end{align*} Thus, by re-substituting the appropriate quantities in~\eqref{eqn:indicator-splitting-for-expectation} and applying the triangle inequality, we have  egin{align} \lefteqn{\ltwo{\E[\optvar_1 - \optvar^*]}} 
onumber \ & \le \ltwo{\E[\invhessian(P + Q)\invhessian\left((P + Q)(\optvar_1 - \optvar^*) -
abla F_1(\optvar^*)ight)]} + \ltwo{\E[\indic{\event^c}(\optvar_1 - \optvar^* - v)]} 
onumber \ & \le \ltwo{\E[\invhessian(P + Q)\invhessian\left((P + Q)(\optvar_1 - \optvar^*) -
abla F_1(\optvar^*)ight)]} + \E[\indic{\event^c} \ltwo{\optvar_1 - \optvar^*}] 
onumber \ & \quad ~ + \E\left[\indic{\event^c} \ltwo{-\invhessian
abla F_1(\optvar^*) + \invhessian(P + Q)\invhessian\left[-
abla F_1(\optvar^*) + (P + Q)(\optvar_1 - \optvar^*)ight]}ight]. \end{align} Since $\ltwo{\optvar_1 - \optvar^*} \le adius$ by assumption, we have  egin{equation*} \E[\indic{\event^c}\ltwo{\optvar_1 - \optvar^*}] \le \P(\event^c) adius \stackrel{(i)}{=} \order(adius 
umobs^{-k/2}) \end{equation*} for any $k \le \min\{\hessmoment, \gradmoment, \objmoment\}$, where step (i) follows from the inequality~\eqref{eqn:no-bad-events}. H"older's inequality also yields that  egin{align*} \lefteqn{\E\left[\indic{\event^c} \ltwo{\invhessian(P + Q) \invhessian 
abla F_1(\optvar^*)}ight] \le \E\left[\indic{\event^c} \matrixnorm{\invhessian(P + Q)}_2 \ltwo{\invhessian 
abla F_1(\optvar^*)}ight]} \ & \qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad \qquad\quad \le \sqrt{\P(\event^c)} \E\left[\matrixnorm{\invhessian(P + Q)}_2^4ight]^{1/4} \E\left[\ltwo{\invhessian 
abla F_1(\optvar^*)}^4ight]^{1/4}. \end{align*} Recalling Lemmas~ef{lemma:moment-consequences} and~ef{lemma:higher-order-matrix-moments}, we have $\E[\matrixnorm{\invhessian(P + Q)}_2^4] = \order(\log^2(d) 
umobs^{-2})$, and we similarly have $\E[\ltwo{\invhessian 
abla F_1(\optvar^*)}^4] = \order(n^{-2})$. Lastly, we have $\P(\event^c) = \order(n^{-k/2})$ for $k \le \min\{\objmoment, \gradmoment, \hessmoment\}$, whence we find that for any such $k$,  egin{equation*} \E\left[\indic{\event^c} \ltwo{\invhessian(P + Q) \invhessian 
abla F_1(\optvar^*)}ight] = \order\left(\sqrt{\log(d)} 
umobs^{-k/4 - 1}ight). \end{equation*} We can similarly apply Lemma~ef{lemma:higher-order-moments} to the last remaining term in the inequality~\eqref{eqn:unbiasing-norms} to obtain that for any $k \le \min\{\hessmoment, \gradmoment, \objmoment\}$,  egin{align*} \E\left[\indic{\event^c} \ltwo{-\invhessian
abla F_1(\optvar^*) + \invhessian(P + Q)\left[-\invhessian

umobs^{-k/2} + 
umobs^{-k/4 - 1}). \end{align*} Applying these two bounds, we find that  egin{equation} \ltwo{\E[\optvar_1 - \optvar^*]} \le \ltwo{\E\left[\invhessian(P + Q)\invhessian\left( (P + Q)(\optvar_1 - \optvar^*) - 
abla F_1(\optvar^*)ight)ight]} + \order(
umobs^{-k}) \end{equation} for any $k$ such that $k \le \min\{\objmoment, \gradmoment, \hessmoment\}/2$ and $k \le \min\{\objmoment, \gradmoment, \hessmoment\}/4 + 1$. In the remainder of the proof, we show that part of the bound~\eqref{eqn:intermediate-norm-expected-bound} still consists only of higher-order terms, leaving us with an expression not involving $\optvar_1 - \optvar^*$. To that end, note that  egin{equation*} \E\left[ \ltwo{\invhessian(P + Q)\invhessian(P + Q)(\optvar_1 - \optvar^*)}^2ight] = \order(
umobs^{-3}) \end{equation*} by three applications of H"older's inequality, the fact that $\ltwo{Ax} \le \matrixnorm{A}_2 \ltwo{x}$, and Lemmas~ef{lemma:moment-consequences},~ef{lemma:higher-order-moments} and~ef{lemma:higher-order-matrix-moments}. Coupled with our bound~\eqref{eqn:intermediate-norm-expected-bound}, we use the fact that $(a + b)^2 \le 2 a^2 + 2 b^2$ to obtain  egin{equation} \ltwo{\E[\optvar_1 - \optvar^*]}^2 \le 2 \ltwo{\E[\invhessian(P + Q) \invhessian 
abla F_1(\optvar^*)]}^2 + \order(
umobs^{-3}). \end{equation} We focus on bounding the remaining expectation. We have the following series of inequalities:  egin{align*} \ltwo{\E[\invhessian(P + Q) \invhessian 
abla F_1(\optvar^*)]} & \stackrel{(i)}{\le} \E\left[\matrixnorm{\invhessian(P + Q)}_2 \ltwo{\invhessian 
abla F_1(\optvar^*)}ight] \ & \stackrel{(ii)}{\le} \left(\E\left[\matrixnorm{\invhessian(P + Q)}_2^2ight] \E\left[\ltwo{\invhessian 
abla F_1(\optvar^*)}^2ight]ight)^{\half} \ & \stackrel{(iii)}{\le} \left(2\E\left[\matrixnorm{\invhessian P}_2^2 + \matrixnorm{\invhessian Q}_2^2ight] \E\left[\ltwo{\invhessian 
abla F_1(\optvar^*)}^2ight]ight)^{\half}. \end{align*} Here step~(i) follows from Jensen's inequality and the fact that $\ltwo{Ax} \le \matrixnorm{A}_2 \ltwo{x}$; step~(ii) uses the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality; and step~(iii) follows from the fact that $(a + b)^2 \le 2a^2 + 2b^2$. We have already bounded the first two terms in the product in our proofs; in particular, Lemma~ef{lemma:moment-consequences} guarantees that $\E[\matrixnorm{P}_2^2] \le C \lipgrad \log d / 
umobs$, while  egin{equation*} \E[\matrixnorm{Q}_2^2] \le \E igg[ rac{1}{
umobs} \sum_{i=1}^n \liphessian(\statrv_i)^4 igg]^\half\ \E[\ltwo{\optvar_1 - \optvar^*}^4]^\half \le C  rac{\liphessian^2 \lipobj^2}{(1 - ho)^2 \strongparam^2} \cdot 
umobs^{-1} \end{equation*} for some numerical constant $C$ (recall Lemma~ef{lemma:higher-order-matrix-moments}). Summarizing our bounds on $\matrixnorm{P}_2$ and $\matrixnorm{Q}_2$, we have  egin{align} \lefteqn{\ltwo{ \E\left[\invhessian(P + Q) \invhessian 
abla F_1(\optvar^*)ight]}^2} 
onumber \ & \le 2 \matrixnorm{\invhessian}_2^2 \left( rac{2 \lipgrad^2(\log d + 1)}{
umobs} + 2 C  rac{\liphessian^2 \lipobj^2}{(1 - ho)^2 \strongparam^2 
umobs} + \order(
umobs^{-2})ight) \E\left[\ltwo{\invhessian 
abla F_1(\optvar^*)}^2ight]. \end{align} From Assumption~ef{assumption:smoothness} we know that $\E[\ltwo{
abla F_1(\optvar^*)}^2] \le \lipobj^2 / n$ and $\matrixnorm{\invhessian}_2 \le 1 / \strongparam$, and hence we can further simplify the bound~\eqref{eqn:matrices-bounded} to obtain  egin{align*} \ltwo{\E[\optvar_1 - \optvar^*]}^2 &\le  rac{C}{\strongparam^2} \left( rac{\lipgrad^2 \log d + \liphessian^2 \lipobj^2 / \strongparam^2 (1 - ho)^2}{
umobs} ight) \E\left[\ltwo{\invhessian 
abla F_1(\optvar^*)}^2ight] + \order(
umobs^{-3})\ &=  rac{C}{\strongparam^2} \left( rac{\lipgrad^2 \log d + \liphessian^2 \lipobj^2 / \strongparam^2 (1 - ho)^2}{
umobs^2} ight) \E\left[\ltwo{\invhessian 
abla f(\optvar^*;X)}^2ight] + \order(
umobs^{-3}) \end{align*} for some numerical constant $C$, where we have applied our earlier inequality~\eqref{eqn:norm-outside-expectation-split}. Noting that we may (without loss of generality) take $ho < \half$, then applying this inequality with the bound~\eqref{eqn:expected-norm-bound} on $\E[\ltwo{\optvar_1 - \optvar^*}^2]$ we previously proved to our decomposition~\eqref{eqn:error-inequality} completes the proof.

nodes.name: Bias/variance decomposition into two lemmas
Optimization error expansion
nodes.statement:
\subsection{Optimization Error Expansion} In this section, we derive a sharper asymptotic expansion of the optimization errors $\optvar_1 - \optvar^*$. Recall our definition of the Kronecker product $\otimes$, where for vectors $u, v$ we have $u \otimes v = u v^	op$. With this notation, we have the following expansion of $\optvar_1 - \optvar^*$. In these lemmas, $emainder_3$ denotes a vector $Z$ for which $\E[\ltwo{Z}^2] \le c n^{-3}$ for a numerical constant $c$.  egin{lemma} Under the conditions of Theorem~ef{theorem:bootstrap}, we have  egin{align} \optvar_1 - \optvar^* & = -\invhessian 
abla F_1(\optvar^*) + \invhessian(
abla^2 F_1(\optvar^*) - \hessian) \invhessian 
abla F_1(\optvar^*) \ & \quad ~ - \invhessian 
abla^3 F_0(\optvar^*)\left( (\invhessian 
abla F_1(\optvar^*)) \otimes (\invhessian 
abla F_1(\optvar^*)) ight)
onumber \ & \quad ~ + \left(\lipthird^2 \lipobj^6 / \strongparam^6 + \lipobj^4 \liphessian^2 d \log(d) / \strongparam^4ight) emainder_3. 
onumber \end{align} \end{lemma} 
oindent We prove Lemma~ef{lemma:first-level-third-order-expansion} in Appendix~ef{sec:proof-third-order-expansion}. The lemma requires careful moment control over the expansion $\optvar_1 - \optvar^*$, leading to some technical difficulty, but is similar in spirit to the results leading to Theorem~ef{theorem:no-bootstrap}. An immediately analogous result to Lemma~ef{lemma:first-level-third-order-expansion} follows for our sub-sampled estimators. Since we use $\ceil{atio 
umobs}$ samples to compute $\optvar_2$, the second level estimator, we find  egin{lemma} Under the conditions of Theorem~ef{theorem:bootstrap}, we have  egin{align*} \optvar_2 - \optvar^* & = -\invhessian 
abla F_2(\optvar^*) + \invhessian(
abla^2 F_2(\optvar^*) - \hessian) \invhessian 
abla F_2(\optvar^*) \ & ~~ - \invhessian 
abla^3 F_0(\optvar^*)\left( (\invhessian 
abla F_2(\optvar^*)) \otimes (\invhessian 
abla F_2(\optvar^*)) ight)\ & ~~ + atio^{- rac{3}{2}} \left(\lipthird^2 \lipobj^6 / \strongparam^6 + \lipobj^4 \liphessian^2 d \log(d) / \strongparam^4ight) emainder_3. \end{align*} \end{lemma}

nodes.name: Bias correction
nodes.statement:
\subsection{Bias Correction} Now that we have given Taylor expansions that describe the behavior of $\optvar_1 - \optvar^*$ and $\optvar_2 - \optvar^*$, we can prove Lemmas~ef{lemma:target-norm-e} and~ef{lemma:target-e-norm} (though, as noted earlier, we defer the proof of Lemma~ef{lemma:target-e-norm} to Appendix~ef{sec:proof-target-e-norm}). The key insight is that expectations of terms involving $
abla F_2(\optvar^*)$ are nearly the same as expectations of terms involving $
abla F_1(\optvar^*)$, except that some corrections for the sampling ratio $atio$ are necessary. We begin by noting that  egin{equation}  rac{\optvar_1 -atio\optvar_2}{1 - atio} - \optvar^* =  rac{\optvar_1 - \optvar^*}{1 - atio} - atio rac{\optvar_2-\optvar^*}{1 - atio}. \end{equation} In Lemmas~ef{lemma:first-level-third-order-expansion} and~ef{lemma:second-level-third-order-expansion}, we derived expansions for each of the right hand side terms, and since  egin{equation*} \E[\invhessian
abla F_1(\optvar^*)] = 0 ~~~ \mbox{and} ~~~ \E[\invhessian
abla F_2(\optvar^*)] = 0, \end{equation*} Lemmas~ef{lemma:first-level-third-order-expansion} and~ef{lemma:second-level-third-order-expansion} coupled with the rewritten correction~\eqref{eqn:separate-combination-to-two-opt-errors} yield  egin{align} \E[\optvar_1 - \optvar^* - atio(\optvar_2-\optvar^*)] & = -atio\E[\invhessian(
abla^2 F_2(\optvar^*) - \hessian) \invhessian 
abla F_2(\optvar^*)] 
onumber \ & \quad ~ + \E[\invhessian(
abla^2 F_1(\optvar^*) - \hessian) \invhessian 
abla F_1(\optvar^*)] 
onumber \ & \quad ~ + atio\E[\invhessian 
abla^3 F_0(\optvar^*)\left( (\invhessian 
abla F_2(\optvar^*)) \otimes (\invhessian 
abla F_2(\optvar^*)) ight)] 
onumber \ & \quad ~ - \E[\invhessian 
abla^3 F_0(\optvar^*)\left( (\invhessian 
abla F_1(\optvar^*)) \otimes (\invhessian 
abla F_1(\optvar^*)) ight)] 
onumber \ & \quad ~ + \order(1) atio^{-1/2}\left( \lipthird^2 \lipobj^6 / \strongparam^6 + \lipobj^4 \liphessian^2 d \log(d) / \strongparam^4ight) 
umobs^{-3/2}. \end{align} Here the remainder terms follow because of the $atio^{-3/2} emainder_3$ term on $\optvar_2 - \optvar^*$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5 (second-order cancellation)
nodes.statement:
\subsection{Proof of Lemma~ef{lemma:target-norm-e}} To prove the claim in the lemma, it suffices to show that  egin{equation} atio\E[\invhessian(
abla^2 F_2(\optvar^*) - \hessian) \invhessian 
abla F_2(\optvar^*)] = \E[\invhessian(

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 6
nodes.statement:
\subsection{Proof of Lemma~ef{lemma:target-e-norm}} The proof of Lemma~ef{lemma:target-e-norm} follows from that of Lemmas~ef{lemma:first-level-third-order-expansion} and~ef{lemma:second-level-third-order-expansion}. We first claim that  egin{equation} \optvar_1-\optvar^* = -\invhessian 
abla F_1(\optvar^*) + emainder_2 ~~~ \mbox{and} ~~~ \optvar_2-\optvar^* = -\invhessian 
abla F_2(\optvar^*) + atio^{-1}emainder_2. \end{equation} The proofs of both claims similar, so we focus on proving the second statement. Using the inequality $(a+b+c)^2\leq 3(a^2+b^2+c^2)$ and Lemma~ef{lemma:second-level-third-order-expansion}, we see that  egin{align} \E\left[\ltwo{\optvar_2-\optvar^* + \invhessian 
abla F_2(\optvar^*)}^2 ight] & \le 3\E\left[\ltwo{\invhessian(
abla^2 F_2(\optvar^*) - \hessian) \invhessian 
abla F_2(\optvar^*)}^2ight] 
onumber\ & ~~ + 3\E\left[\ltwo{\invhessian 
abla^3 F_0(\optvar^*)\left( (\invhessian 
abla F_2(\optvar^*)) \otimes (\invhessian 
abla F_2(\optvar^*)) ight)}^2ight] 
onumber\ & ~~ + 3 atio^{-3} \order(
umobs^{-3}). \end{align} We now bound the first two terms in inequality~\eqref{eqn:bootstrap-e-norm-expansion-bound}. Applying the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality and Lemma~ef{lemma:moment-consequences}, the first term can be upper bounded as  egin{align*} \lefteqn{\E\left[\ltwo{\invhessian(
abla^2 F_2(\optvar^*) - \hessian) \invhessian 
abla F_2(\optvar^*)}^2ight]} \ & \le \left(\E\left[\matrixnorm{\invhessian (
abla^2 F_2(\optvar^*) - \hessian)}_2^4ight] \E\left[\ltwo{\invhessian 
abla F_2(\optvar^*)}^4ight]ight)^{1/2} \ & = \left(atio^{-2})\order(\log^2(d) 
umobs^{-2}) \cdot atio^{-2} \order(
umobs^{-2})ight)^{1/2} \; = \; atio^{-2} \order(n^{-2}), \end{align*} where the order notation subsumes the logarithmic factor in the dimension. Since $
abla^3 F_0(\optvar^*) : \R^{d^2} ightarrow \R^d$ is linear, the second term in the inequality~\eqref{eqn:bootstrap-e-norm-expansion-bound} may be bounded completely analogously as it involves the outer product $\invhessian 
abla F_2(\optvar^*) \otimes \invhessian 
abla F_2(\optvar^*)$. Recalling the bound~\eqref{eqn:bootstrap-e-norm-expansion-bound}, we have thus shown that  egin{equation*} \E\left[\ltwo{\optvar_2-\optvar^* + \invhessian 
abla F_2(\optvar^*)}^2 ight] = atio^{-2} \order(
umobs^{-2}), \end{equation*} or $\optvar_2 - \optvar^* = -\invhessian

Now we turn to controlling the rate at which $\optvar^t - \eta_t \gradient_t$ goes to zero. Let $f_t(\cdot) = f(\cdot; \statrv_t)$ be shorthand for the loss evaluated on the $t^{th}$ data point. By defining  egin{align*} r_t = g_t -

abla^2 f_t(\optvar^*)$ is (conditionally) independent of $\optvar^t$ and  egin{equation} \E[\gradient_t] =

Applying Assumption~ef{assumption:smoothness-sgd} and H"older's inequality, we find that since $\optvar^t$ is conditionally independent of $\statrv_t$,  egin{align*} \E\left[\ltwo{r_t \indic{\optvar^t \in U_ho}}ight] & \le \E\left[ \matrixnorm{

ot\in U_ho}}ight] \stackrel{(i)}{\le} \sqrt[4]{\E[\ltwo{r_t}^4]} \left(\P(\optvar^t

By combining the expansion~\eqref{eqn:sgd-truncate-grad} with the bound~\eqref{eqn:sgd-rt-bound}, we find that  egin{align*} \lefteqn{\ltwo{\E[\optvar^t - \eta_t \gradient_t - \optvar^*]} = \ltwo{\E[(I - \eta_t 
abla^2 F_0(\optvar^*))(\optvar^t - \optvar^*) + \eta_t r_t]}} \ & \qquad \qquad \le \ltwo{\E[(I - \eta_t

abla^t F_0(\optvar^*)}_2 \ltwo{\E[\optvar^t - \optvar^*]} +  rac{c \alpha^{3/4} \lipobj^{3/2}}{\strongparam^{5/2} t^{7/4}} \!\left( rac{\alpha^{1/4}\liphessian \lipobj^{1/2}}{\strongparam^{1/2} t^{1/4}} +  rac{4 \lipobj + \lipgrad adius}{ho^{3/2}}ight)\!. \end{equation*} We now complete the proof via an inductive argument using our immediately preceding bounds. Our reasoning follows a similar induction given by~\citet{RakhlinShSr12}. First, note that by strong convexity and our condition that $\matrixnorm{
abla^2 F_0(\optvar^*)} \le \lipgrad$, we have  egin{equation*} \matrixnorm{I - \eta_t

abla^2 F_0(\optvar^*) \le 1 - \eta_t \strongparam \end{equation*} whenever $1 - \eta_t \lipgrad \ge 0$. Define $	au_0 = \ceil{c \lipgrad / \strongparam}$; then for $t \ge t_0$ we obtain  egin{equation} \ltwo{\E[\optvar^{t+1}-\optvar^*]} \le (1-c/t)\ltwo{\E[\optvar^t-\optvar^*]} +  rac{1}{t^{7/4}} \cdot  rac{c \alpha^{3/4} \lipobj^{3/2}}{\strongparam^{5/2}} \left( rac{\alpha^{1/4}\liphessian \lipobj^{1/2}}{\strongparam^{1/2} t^{1/4}} +  rac{4 \lipobj + \lipgrad adius}{ho^{3/2}}ight). \end{equation} For shorthand, we define two intermediate variables  egin{align*} a_{t}= \ltwo{\E(\optvar^{t}-\optvar^*)} ~~~\mbox{and}~~~ b =  rac{c \alpha^{3/4} \lipobj^{3/2}}{\strongparam^{5/2}} \left( rac{\alpha^{1/4}\liphessian \lipobj^{1/2}}{\strongparam^{1/2}} +  rac{4 \lipobj + \lipgrad adius}{ho^{3/2}}ight). \end{align*} Inequality \eqref{eqn:sgd-induction} then implies the inductive relation $a_{t+1}\leq (1-c/t)a_t + b/t^{7/4}$. Now we show that by defining $ eta = \max\{	au_0 adius, b / (c - 1)\}$, we have $a_t \le  eta / t^{3/4}$. Indeed, it is clear that $a_1 \le 	au_0 adius$. nodes.statement:
The proof follows from a slightly more careful application of the Taylor expansion~\eqref{eqn:taylor-error-expansion}. The starting point in our proof is to recall the success events~\eqref{eqn:good-events} and the joint event $\event \defeq \event_0 \cap \event_1 \cap \event_2$. We begin by arguing that we may focus on the case where $\event$ holds. Let $C$ denote the right hand side of the equality~\eqref{eqn:third-order-expansion} except for the remainder $emainder_3$ term. By Assumption~ef{assumption:smoothness}, we follow the bound~\eqref{eqn:no-bad-events} (with $\min\{\objmoment, \gradmoment, \hessmoment\} \ge 8$) to find that  egin{equation*} \E\left[\indic{\event^c} \ltwo{\optvar_1 - \optvar^*}^2ight] = \order\left(adius^2 
umobs^{-4}ight), \end{equation*} so we can focus on the case where the joint event $\event = \event_0 \cap \event_1 \cap \event_2$ does occur. Defining $\optvarerr = \optvar_1 - \optvar^*$ for notational convenience, on $\event$ we have that for some $\interp \in [0, 1]$, with $\optvar' = (1 - \interp) \optvar_1 + \interp \optvar^*$,  egin{align*} 0 & =

abla^2 F_0(\optvar^*)$, the Hessian of the risk at the optimal point, and solve for the error $\optvarerr$ to see that  egin{align} \optvarerr & = -\invhessian

As we did in the proof of Theorem~ef{theorem:no-bootstrap}, specifically in deriving the recursive equality~\eqref{eqn:recursive-equality}, we may apply the expansion~\eqref{eqn:simple-error-expansion} of $\optvarerr = \optvar_1 - \optvar^*$ to obtain a clean asymptotic expansion of $\optvarerr$ using~\eqref{eqn:third-order-taylor-expansion}. abla F_1(\optvar^*)) \otimes (\invhessian
